title: Adult Nursing in the UK for International Students
excerpt: Want to become a nurse in the UK? See adult nursing course routes, English requirements, NMC registration, placements, costs and visa rules for 2027 entry.

Routes Into Adult Nursing

To work as a registered nurse in the UK you must complete an approved nursing program and then register with the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC). International students usually choose between two routes.

RouteLengthWho it suits
BSc (Hons) Adult Nursing3 yearsStudents entering after high school or access courses
MSc Adult Nursing (pre-registration)About 2 yearsGraduates in a related subject

Entry and English Requirements

  • Academic: recent high school or degree results in relevant subjects; some courses prefer biology or health science.
  • English: nursing courses ask for higher scores than most degrees, typically around IELTS 7.0 overall with no less than 6.5 in any part. Check each university.
  • Suitability checks: interviews, health clearance and criminal record checks are common.
  • Experience: caring experience helps your personal statement.
⚠️
Not every course is open to international studentsSome universities limit international places for nursing, so apply early and confirm eligibility before paying a deposit.

Placements and Registration

Nursing programs include around 2,300 hours of clinical practice in hospitals and community settings, shared with classroom study. After graduation you apply to the NMC to join the register, which is required to practice as a nurse.

Costs, Visa and Careers After Study

Tuition for international nursing students is often around £15,000 to £22,000 a year; confirm the exact fee for your course. Student visa maintenance funds are £1,171/£1,529 per month now, rising to £1,203/£1,570 from 30 November 2026, for up to nine months. A Student visa lets you work up to 20 hours a week in term time, but placement hours are part of your course.

After graduating, you may use the Graduate Route (18 months for applications from 1 January 2027) or move to a Health and Care Worker visa if a UK employer sponsors you as a registered nurse.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can international students study adult nursing in the UK?
Yes, though places for international students can be limited. Check each university's policy.
Do I need NMC registration?
Yes. You must register with the NMC after graduation to practice as a registered nurse in the UK.
Will I get a job after graduating?
Demand for nurses is high, but sponsorship depends on the employer and visa rules at the time. Check current rules.
